minutes.headline: Committee approved the LEA stipend agreement, a 125-student extended day cap, and revised facility field fees.
minutes.summary: After an executive session on non-union negotiations, the committee heard the superintendent's report, athletics participation trends, and a budget update. It discussed the FY21 budget timeline, school choice data, and a new fundraising process. It voted on handbooks, an LEA agreement, extended day caps and facility fees.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved a memorandum of agreement with the Lunenburg Education Association; stipended positions were kept using non-monetary compensation.
The committee capped extended day at 125 students per day, with 126 allowed on Thursdays, and families will be told registration closes September 30.
The committee approved the facility fees schedule as presented, after the director proposed lower hourly rates for grass fields.
The FY21 budget presentation will move to January or February to wait for the governor's numbers; initiatives are still presented in December.
The committee accepted the budget update and the personnel update, which passed with one abstention.

why_it_matters: The extended day cap limits how many children can be enrolled each day, which affects families who rely on the program for child care.
Field fee rates decide what youth sports groups pay to use school fields, and the later budget timeline means the FY21 school budget and its effect on taxes will come into focus later than usual.
watch_next: The business manager's report on school choice student data, due in the coming weeks.
The FY21 budget presentation to the committee in January or February, after the governor's numbers are released.
